resource_contract.actions: Only the two frozen amplitudes, old and new, with common duration1, and the existing spectator_plus or spectator_0 preparations. Each execution returns the complete three-bit outcome and costs one. Fresh shot noise is independent; no hidden-noise coupling.
resource_contract.expanded_hamiltonian: H(u)=((omega+u)/2)X_0+(gamma+chi*u)P11_(1,2). Unknown fixed real omega,gamma,chi; fixed Markov/readout nuisance may also be unknown. The witness uses omega=0,kappa=0,readout=1/200 in both worlds.
resource_contract.good_world: chi=0, gamma=2 asin(sqrt(t_good)); spectators are exactly invariant under the two amplitudes.
resource_contract.null_world: chi=(2 asin(sqrt(t_null))-2 asin(sqrt(t_good)))/(u_new-u_old), gamma=2 asin(sqrt(t_good))-chi*u_old. All coefficients are fixed before observations, so this is a single amplitude-dependent Hamiltonian, not freely assigned arm probabilities.
resource_contract.shared_information: Controls, target task, complete bitstrings and the declared enlarged Hamiltonian family are identical for both worlds and all algorithms. Hidden omega/gamma/chi are never supplied to the validator.
resource_contract.not_covered: Additional amplitudes, durations, spectator probes, known chi=0, or a sufficiently restrictive prior bound on chi change the information experiment; this lower bound does not cover them.

exact_output_laws.factorization: q0 is independent of the spectator pair because the two Hamiltonian terms commute on disjoint subsystems; independent readout preserves factorization. Spectator_0 is blind to P11 in either world.

analytic_lower_bound.proof: Old and spectator_0 laws coincide between good and null worlds. Only new spectator_plus shots contribute KL=D(Q_good||Q_null). For any predictable randomized allocation and finite stopping time, transcript KL=E_good[N_new_target]*D. Data processing of accept implies transcript KL>=kl(.95,.01). Therefore E_good[N_total]>=E_good[N_new_target]>=kappa/D.
analytic_lower_bound.scope: This is a necessary cost at the good world for a validator uniformly1percent-risk-valid over the expanded physical crosstalk class, with95percent correct acceptance at that good world. It is not a lower bound for a validator allowed to assume chi=0.

common_Q_control.rule: Observe old/new X0 outcomes with independent shot noise; multiply L+ by1.5 on(old1,new0),by.5 on(old0,new1),and by1 otherwise. L- swaps those factors. Accept/reject on the respective first crossing of200; stop at cap if neither crosses.
common_Q_control.risk: When x_old<=x_new, L+ is a nonnegative supermartingale; when x_old>=x_new, L- is. Under equality their union crossing probability is<=.01. With common spectator success s>0 these are exactly the target sign nulls.
common_Q_control.cost_and_power_proof: In the good world, log L+ has the displayed positive mean increment and positive overshoot<=log1.5. Stopped Wald gives E[T+] <=(log200+log1.5)/drift. Stopping at either sign and capping reduce expected cost. Wrong-sign probability<=.005 and Markov cap abstention<=E[T+]/cap_pairs give the correct-stop lower bound.
common_Q_control.scope: Classical fixed-alternative conditional McNemar/SPRT control, not a new FaultTune method or full-field SOTA winner.

invariance_tax.exact_acceptance_failure_when_ignoring_s: The entire X0-only history has the identical law in both worlds. Thus the common-Q control accepts the null world with probability at least its good-world correct-stop lower bound, exceeding95percent. It cannot be promoted as robust to unknown amplitude crosstalk.
invariance_tax.interpretation: The large bitstring gain depends materially on the model promise. Uniform validity over a larger physically plausible family can force an order-of-magnitude larger cost even at a truly invariant point. This is a cross-model cost separation, not a same-model algorithm speedup.

high_precision_physical_parameters_diagn.scope: Angle decimals only verify the analytic exact inverse-trigonometric construction. Rational PMFs and directed KL bounds carry the cost statement.

claim_boundary: No Monte Carlo, no SOTA gain, no reclassification of an old failed candidate, and no claim that all full-bitstring mechanisms fail. The useful invariant-family shortcut and the expanded-family obstruction are distinct statements.
